To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the combination of honeypots with specific reverse engineering features allows the capture of malicious entities and the automatic analysis of their behavior, thus enabling the identification of the malware family to which they belong and the detection of the malicious activities they are capable of performing.

(1) high-interaction honepots can be enhanced with features that allow to capture and analyze malicious entities in the context of their propagation; (2) the proposed features can be used to reverse engineer malware, and (3) the resulting malware reverse engineering framework is effective, as shown by a case study.

a honeypot can be used to: • Capture malware samples, • Analyze malware samples, • Identify the presence of malware in the honeypot, • Detect and prevent the propagation of malware in the network, • Detect the presence of malware that has been already installed in other systems, • Analyze the behavior of malware, and, • Identify the malware’s target.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design and development of a new generation of honeypots that can be effectively used to reverse engineer malicious entities and, in general, to analyze the behavior of malware.
the development of an architecture that integrates a high-interaction honeynet with a reverse engineering environment, and with the implementation and testing of the resulting system.

the following questions: 1) How to improve the reverse engineering of malicious entities? 2) How to use a high-interaction honeynet to capture and analyze malicious entities? 3) How to improve honeypot-powered reverse engineering? 4) How to improve reverse engineering of malware by using high-interaction honeynets?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the research presented in this thesis shows how high-interactivity honeypots can effectively support the reverse-engineering activities of malware.

the research presented in this work has demonstrated that honeypots, in particular high-interaction honepots, can be used as an effective and efficient technology to capture, analyze and study the behavior of malware.

the proposed approach is able to effectively and efficiently reverse engineer the malware and the malicious network traffic generated by it, and to provide an effective and efficient analysis of its behaviors and effects on a system, in a fully automatic and unattended fashion.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we are proposing an architecture and a set of tools to enhance the analysis of malware that propagate through networks, and to provide an improved understanding of their behaviors, and their impact on the target system.

we have designed and implemented a high-interaction honeynet that is able to capture and store malware samples in a safe environment, and to perform a reverse engineering process that allows the identification of malware characteristics and behaviors.
we have developed a new approach to the design and implementation of high-interaction honepots that allows us to perform a more detailed analysis of the behaviors of the malicious entities captured.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, by using a honeypot, it is possible to obtain a more complete view of the malware behavior, which is not possible by using only a standard virtualized environment.

, when properly enhanced with specific reverse engineering features and capabilities, honeypots are able to support the reverse engineering activities that are needed to understand the behavior of malware, to detect its effects on the system and to assess its potential impact.

the use of honeypots in the context of malware reverse engineering is a promising approach to improve the efficiency of such activities, which are currently carried out in a manual and time-consuming manner.
